# tfctl CLI Overview

The tfctl CLI is a command-line interface tool that enables you to interact with HCP Terraform programmatically. Use tfctl to automate workflows, manage runs, configure variables, and perform API operations directly from your terminal.

## Introduction

The tfctl CLI provides a streamlined interface for common HCP Terraform operations. It simplifies authentication, run management, and API interactions, making it easier to integrate HCP Terraform into your automation pipelines and development workflows.

## Workflows

The following sections describe the primary workflows for using tfctl.

### Getting started

To begin using tfctl, complete the following steps:

1. Install tfctl on your local machine or CI/CD environment.
1. Authenticate with HCP Terraform using your credentials.
1. Configure your profile settings to specify default organizations and workspaces.

Refer to the [Install](/terraform/tfctl-cli/install) and [Authenticate](/terraform/tfctl-cli/authenticate) pages for detailed instructions.

### Managing runs

To manage Terraform runs using tfctl:

- Start new runs in your workspaces.
- Check the status of running or completed runs.
- Monitor run progress and outcomes.

### Working with variables

tfctl enables you to manage workspace variables:

- Import variables from configuration files.
- Update variable values programmatically.
- Manage sensitive variables securely.

### Constraints and limitations

- tfctl requires HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise.
- Some commands require specific permissions in your HCP Terraform organization.
- API rate limits apply to tfctl operations.

## Contributing

The tfctl CLI is open source. To contribute to the project or build from source, visit the [tfctl-cli repository on GitHub](https://github.com/hashicorp/tfctl-cli). The repository includes detailed developer documentation, contribution guidelines, and instructions for building from source.
